note: One record per work quoted in data/quotes.json. A work's subject is its field, taken from SUBJECTS in assets/quote-core.js, and it is assigned here once per book rather than per quote — a couple of dozen entries someone can check against a library record instead of a couple of hundred readings nobody can. Era is not stored: it is computed from `year`, so it cannot drift from the date. Since 2026-09-16 the registry is also his library rather than only his citations: a book he owns or wants carries `shelf` (read, reading, to-read, abandoned), `rating` 0–10 for how good it was, `want` 0–10 for how much he wants to read it, `pages`, its `goodreads` id and isbn, the `added` and `read` dates, and `cover` — a front cover under assets/covers/ with `coverSize` as [width, height] so the page can reserve its box before the image loads, and `coverSource` recording where the picture came from, so a wrong one can be traced. A work with a shelf but no quotes is a book on the shelf, not an error. `url` is present only where the primary text has a stable home; everything else gets a find-it link generated from its year on works.html.
